sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at a 20.5% CAGR to $155.2 billion, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2024 was the step change: revenue rose 15.7% to $245.1 billion, driven by growth across each segment, with Gaming up 39% on the Activision Blizzard acquisition [F8][D364][P33][P26].
FY2026 accelerated again, revenue up 17.8% to $331.8 billion on Microsoft Cloud growth, with Intelligent Cloud up 29.7% on Azure [F10][D472][P17][D916].
Microsoft Cloud reached $214.4 billion, 64.6% of revenue, and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% FY2026 growth [S24][D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose 31% to $129.4 billion, driven by Azure and other cloud services growing 41% [S61][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added $14.2 billion, a 5.1pp contribution, on Copilot and E5 revenue per user [S64][D649][P14].
Operating income grew 20.8% against 17.8% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against 31.3% net income growth, with the share count down only 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is the window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below the 68.2% median, as cost of revenue rose 21.1% and took 0.9pp off operating margin [F30][D486][D981][D489][D500].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue, the window low, and added 0.8pp to margin as operating expenses grew 7.4% [D450][D985][D501][D491].
Net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below operating margin, helped by $6.5 billion of OpenAI investment gains in other income [F70][F50][D1023][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, 55.1% of revenue, on higher customer cash receipts and lower tax payments [F100][D477][D457][P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, a 20.2% margin and the window low, as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion [F120][D478][D456][D982][F110][D479].
Free cash flow covered only 0.50x of net income, the window low against a 0.91x median, and capex ran 3.38x D&A [D460][D988][D990][D461].
Investing cash use rose $66.9 billion, mainly a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions and $22.2 billion for component purchases [P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion, and the current ratio of 1.23x is the window low [D464][D495][D463][D494][F200][D991].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion used 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
Return on average equity of 34.0% sits at the peer median of 38.8%, below the FY2022 peak of 47.2% [D471][D1011][D257].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the lowest in the window [R1][D406][D460][D988].
The gap is capex-led, with additions to property and equipment up $51.4 billion in FY2026, so it reflects AI buildout rather than weak collections [P1].
FY2017 short-term investments were not reported, so cash and investments and net cash omit them that year [R6][X158].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, and the pack uses first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
If FY2027 capex as a share of revenue stays at or above the FY2026 34.9%, free cash flow margin likely stays near the 20.2% low [D455][D456].
A recovery in free cash flow per net income back toward the 0.91x median would confirm the capex cycle is peaking [D990].
Watch operating margin against the 46.8% high; a drop toward the 41.7% median would signal AI infrastructure costs outrunning cloud growth [F50][D975].
